name: Pixxel Firefly Constellation

header.one_liner: Pixxel's Firefly satellites form a commercial hyperspectral Earth-observation constellation delivering ~5 m resolution across 150+ spectral bands; the first three launched in January 2025.
header.indigenous_label: Indian-founded (Bengaluru operations); US-incorporated HQ — no audited indigenous percentage

what_it_is.prose: Firefly is the commercial hyperspectral Earth-observation constellation built by Pixxel, an Indian-founded company with operations in Bengaluru and a US-incorporated headquarters. Each Firefly satellite images in more than 150 narrow spectral bands at roughly 5 m spatial resolution — about six times sharper than legacy 30 m hyperspectral systems — over a ~40 km swath from a sun-synchronous orbit near 550 km. The first three operational Fireflies launched on 14–15 January 2025 aboard SpaceX's Transporter-12 rideshare from Vandenberg Space Force Base (integrated by Exolaunch), and Pixxel announced 'first light' hyperspectral imagery in March 2025, with additional Fireflies following later in 2025 to build toward daily global coverage. The hyperspectral data targets agriculture, forestry, mining, environmental and climate monitoring, water quality and government applications. Pixxel is among the best-funded hyperspectral startups globally. This dossier records the launched, operational constellation and keeps the final constellation size and India-specific procurement open pending primary disclosure.

import_dependencies.summary: Pixxel has not published a component sovereignty breakdown. As with most EO smallsats, space-grade detectors/optics and radiation-tolerant electronics are potential import exposures; launch to date has used a US provider (SpaceX).
